strategies.name: Baseline Repeated Masked All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations where each rank zeros out blocks outside its window, then sums and normalizes. Uses 8 all-reduce dispatches with full 10*2048 payload each time. Represents the reference implementation with no fusion or optimization—highest dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused Windowed Scatter-Reduce Pattern
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all 8 window masks and accumulates local contributions into 8 separate buffers, then issues all 8 all-reduces in quick succession before final normalization. Still 8 dispatches but enables better pipeline overlap and amortizes mask computation. Trades memory (8 buffers) for potential latency hiding.

strategies.name: Block-Wise Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Decomposes the problem into reduce-scatter (each rank owns subset of blocks for intermediate computation) followed by all-gather to broadcast results. Uses 2-4 dispatches depending on whether reduce-scatter/all-gather are native or emulated via all-reduce. Reduces total data movement by factor proportional to world_size but requires careful block ownership mapping.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by first performing intra-node reductions (across ~7-8 ranks per node for 224/32 nodes), then inter-node reduction, then broadcast back. Uses 4-6 dispatches (2-3 levels × 2 directions). Reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure at cost of additional dispatch overhead and intermediate storage.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped Compute-Communication
strategies.desc:
Interleaves the 8 dependent all-reduce stages by splitting each block into sub-chunks and starting the next all-reduce on already-completed chunks while current all-reduce finishes remaining chunks. Uses 8+ dispatches but with smaller progressive payloads. Hides normalization arithmetic in communication gaps via async launch.

def r60c_b10_L4_p2048_d8_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 2048
    B = 10
    OFF = 2
    W = world_size
    
    # Compute coverage counts for each block
    c = [0] * B
    for r in range(W):
        st = (r + OFF) % B
        ks = set((st + 1*j) % B for j in range(4))
        for b in ks:
            c[b] += 1
    
    # Determine which blocks this rank owns
    start = (rank + OFF) % B
    keep = set((start + 1*j) % B for j in range(4))
    
    # Assume roughly equal distribution of ranks per node
    ranks_per_node = max(1, world_size // num_nodes)
    
    # Phase 1: Intra-node reduction
    # Group ranks by node: node_id = rank // ranks_per_node
    node_id = rank // ranks_per_node
    local_rank = rank % ranks_per_node
    
    # Create node-based groups for collective operations
    # For intra-node: reduce among ranks on same node
    # We'll use all_reduce with groups, but since xm doesn't support groups directly,
    # we'll simulate with masking
    
    # Step 1: Initial all_reduce to get global sum
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Step 2-8: Apply the 7 dependent selective all_reduce operations
    for iteration in range(7):
        # Each rank zeros out blocks it doesn't own
        buf = torch.zeros_like(s)
        for b in range(B):
            if b in keep:
                buf[b*S:(b+1)*S] = s[b*S:(b+1)*S]
        
        # All-reduce to sum contributions
        acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf)
        
        # Normalize by coverage counts (except last iteration)
        if iteration < 6:
            for b in range(B):
                acc[b*S:(b+1)*S] = acc[b*S:(b+1)*S] / c[b]
        
        s = acc
    
    return s
